name: Document comparison matrix
description: Comparison matrix in the document: columns are optional solutions, rows are capabilities or differences, supports four values ​​✓ / — / ◐ part / text, can be arranged by group, click on the column header to highlight a solution.
scenarios: Compare installation methods such as desktop version, local browser version and source code running
Compare Page and Board, export format, Agent access method and other options
List the extent to which different solutions support a certain capability

boundaries: Used for qualitative comparison of 2–6 solutions in ShowAI documents in several dimensions; each box is yes / no / part / a short text.
It is not used for numerical data or large tables that require sorting and filtering; use charts or built-in tables for numerical comparison.
Read-only display: Clicking on the column header only changes the local view and does not modify the page data.

usage.purpose: Help readers choose between several solutions: see at a glance what each solution supports, what it does not support, and where it falls short.
structure: Each column in the header has a solution: color point, name and a line of description; click on the column header to highlight the light color of the entire column, and click again to cancel.
The first column is the comparison item (name and small text prompt), which is fixed to the left when scrolling horizontally.
Rows with the same group are grouped together, with the group name as the group title; the groups are arranged in the order of first occurrence.

Grid: true displays the check mark of the scheme color, false displays a light-colored dash, "partial" displays a semicircle and "partial", and other strings are displayed as text according to inline markers.
There can be a line of notes below the table. When the screen is narrow, the table scrolls horizontally, and the right side fades to indicate that there are more columns.

inputs.meaning: Scheme columns, arranged in order of display. 2–4 columns are recommended, with a maximum of 8 columns; 3 columns and above require horizontal scrolling in the width of mobile phones.
Column identifier, referenced in rows[].values ​​and highlight, unique within the same table.
The plan name is displayed in the header and should be short (no more than 8 Chinese characters).
A line of additional description for the scheme, shown below the name.
Column colors: color points, checkmarks, partial support icons, and highlight background colors. brand | teal | warm | violet | rose | slate.
Contrasted items, displayed in order; rows in the same group converge to the first occurrence of the group. Maximum 80 lines, no more than 20 lines recommended.
Small text description below the comparison item supports inline markup.
Group name; rows with the same name are grouped under the same group heading.

omission.description: The row does not belong to any group and appears with other ungrouped rows without a group title.

inputs.meaning: Values ​​with column id as the key: true = supported (check mark), false = not supported (dash), "partial" = partially supported, other strings = text description (inline mark supported). If a column's key is missing, the field is left blank (shows a shallow dot); keys that do not belong to any column are ignored and readData is listed in unknownColumnKeys.
Initial highlighted column id. Readers can still click on the column header to switch or cancel.
A line of description or source below the table, supporting inline markup and document links.

recipes.title: Write a plan comparison
steps: First determine the choices the reader has to make, list 2–4 solutions as columns, and give each solution a tone.

Write a difference that the reader cares about in each line; use true/false if it can be expressed as yes/no, use "partial" if it is conditional and explain the condition in hint, and use a short sentence for the rest.
If there are more than 6 lines, use group to divide them into 2-4 groups; fill in the id of the recommended solution in highlight.
Checking with readData that unknownColumnKeys is empty and the supported/partial/unsupported counts for each column are as expected.

interactions.action: Click or use the keyboard to activate column headers
interactions.effect: The entire column is highlighted with a light color of the column color; activating it again cancels it.

interactions.action: Horizontal scrolling of tables on narrow screens
interactions.effect: The first column is fixed on the left and fades out on the right to indicate that there are more columns.

interactions.action: Click on a link in the grid or description
interactions.effect: The link is opened by the host; the document site link is opened within the site.

constraints: Reading operations do not modify page data.
The content of the grid should be short: within one sentence; long explanations should be placed in the text or notes outside the table.

When the width is less than 640px, the first column is narrowed to 116px, and each column is at least 112px: a 390px wide screen can fully display 2 columns, and 3 columns or more can be scrolled horizontally.

data: When adding or deleting columns, the key and highlight of each row's values ​​are updated simultaneously.
To change the grouping, just modify rows[].group.
implementation: New value types (such as numeric values ​​or ratings) require a new version and updated readData.

entryPoints.purpose: Components, grouping sections(), value mark Mark, inline mark md() and readData.
Design tokens (including dark colors), tables, fixed first column, column protrusion, horizontal scrolling fade and narrow screen rules.

architecture: Use semantic <table>: buttons in table header th[scope=col] switch highlighted columns, row header th[scope=row], one <tbody> for each group.

Highlighting a column is achieved by adding the is-on class to each cell of the column (including the space of the group header row), so the background color runs through the entire height of the column.
The scroll container monitors scroll and ResizeObserver, calculates whether it can still scroll to the right, and controls the fade-out prompt and the first column separator.
extensionPoints: Color is mapped to the two variables --tc / --ts by tone; the new value types are expanded in kindOf and Mark.
invariants: The component does not call onChange; all interactions only change local state.
Do not use dangerouslySetInnerHTML; inline markup is generated by md() React elements.
verification: Example 0: 3 columns, 8 rows, 3 groups, the local browser version is initially highlighted; desktop supported=3, unsupported=3 in readData.
Check header, ticks, section support and horizontal scroll fade in 1000 px, 390 px width and dark theme.
